item.title: Unseen Efforts: Disparities in Unpaid Care Work Before and After COVID-19 - IWPR
item.description: The COVID-19 pandemic brought to the fore the need for unpaid care work, as well as the highly unequal distribution of care work. This study contributes to the understanding of care work by providing post-COVID assessments of changes in unpaid caregiving by gender, race/ethnicity, and socioeconomic status. DOWNLOAD REPORT The post Unseen Efforts: Disparities in Unpaid Care Work Before and After COVID-19 appeared first on IWPR.

item.title: The Numbers Don’t Add Up: Women Continue to Earn Less, Regardless of Occupation - IWPR
item.description: In 2025, women were paid less than men for full-time work in all 20 occupations that employ the most women and in all 20 occupations that employ the most men in the United States. Across all detailed occupations with sufficient data, women were paid up to $846 less per week compared to men in the same occupation.
